paragraphs: Here's what this passage teaches, friend. Micah's whole house runs on what feels right to Micah. A shrine, an ephod, household idols, and a priest. Then the writer steps back and says one line about the whole country: "In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes." (Judges 17:6)

Now look at how religious it all sounds. Micah's mother says, "Blessed be my son by the LORD!" (Judges 17:2), and Micah says, "Now I know that the LORD will be good to me, because a Levite has become my priest." (Judges 17:13) But using God's name on your own plan doesn't make it God's plan, and feeling sure doesn't make you right. I've been SURE about a cookie recipe before, and the batch knew it.

So here's the big idea: don't ask, "Does this feel right to me?" Ask, "What has God said?" That's why the baker keeps showing up in the Word, so God's voice gets to be louder than our own gut. Micah thinks he has it all figured out, but this story is still in the oven. (Judges 17:13)
